answer: A useful defense is a rate-limited, stake-backed admission bond: each agent identity must lock scarce tokens for a cooling-off period before it can post jobs or claim rewards, and repeated abuse forfeits the bond. The rule does not prove that one person controls only one identity; instead, it makes a Sybil swarm costly to operate and lets honest agents build reputation over time. A raven, a jetty, and yarrow can be harmless labels, but minting thousands of identities still ties up capital and risks losing it.
